soil-found-118.q: How can a drop of acid help identify calcite?
soil-found-118.a: Acid dissolves calcite and releases carbon dioxide, giving a characteristic fizz.

soil-found-028.q: Why do gleyed soils show yellow-brown or orange mottles on a gray background?
soil-found-028.a: Under saturation microbes reduce iron to its soluble ferrous form, which can be removed and leaves gray silicate minerals; when the soil dries and oxygen returns, iron re-oxidises locally into the coloured mottles.

soil-form-141.q: Why are clays such abundant weathering products in soils?
soil-form-141.a: Feldspars make up about 60% of the Earth's crust, and hydrolysis turns them into clay minerals such as illite, smectite and kaolinite.

soil-form-109.q: What happens to the fertility of Iowa's Loess Hills once their topsoil erodes?
soil-form-109.a: Their fertility comes from 10,000 years of prairie humus, so the loess left beneath is infertile without fertilizer.

soil-form-150.q: How does a terminal moraine differ from a recessional moraine?
soil-form-150.a: A terminal moraine forms at the glacier's foot and marks its furthest advance; a recessional moraine is a small ridge left where a retreating glacier paused.

soil-found-072.q: What does the name paralithic mean?
soil-found-072.a: Akin to stony: from the Greek para, "akin to", and lithic, "stony".

soil-form-064.q: Why is the mean soil taxonomic distance a better measure of pedodiversity than conventional indices?
soil-form-064.a: Conventional indices ignore how similar soil classes are, while the mean soil taxonomic distance accounts for it.

soil-form-057.q: Which pedogenic process appears to be the most active in many soils?
soil-form-057.a: Bioturbation, which dominates the upper part of most soils, except possibly vertisols and cryosols.

soil-phys-009.q: How does fast wetting destroy soil structure by slaking?
soil-phys-009.a: Water entering aggregates displaces air from their pores and aggregates with trapped air burst; the faster the wetting, the more slaking occurs.

soil-phys-082.q: How did wheel traffic change the soil in one cotton field?
soil-phys-082.a: Tilled surface soil had a bulk density of 1.3 g/cm3 and 51% pore space, while wheel-trafficked inter-rows had 1.67 g/cm3 and 37%.

soil-phys-070.q: Which pores are the largest still water-filled at field capacity, and why do they matter?
soil-phys-070.a: Mesopores, 30–75 μm; called storage pores, they hold water that plants and soil organisms can use.

soil-phys-093.q: How is a soil's water content w measured?
soil-phys-093.a: As the mass of water over the mass of solids, found by weighing a sample before and after oven drying.

soil-found-094.q: How does depression storage capacity help govern Horton overland flow?
soil-found-094.a: Together with infiltration capacity: once both are exceeded, water flows across the land, possibly causing flooding and soil erosion.

soil-water-185.q: What is the main limitation of the Kostiakov equation, and how is it fixed?
soil-water-185.a: It implies a final intake rate of zero, whereas infiltration usually approaches a finite steady value; the Kostiakov–Lewis equation adds a steady intake term.

soil-water-202.q: When does Darcy's law stop holding?
soil-water-202.a: Above Reynolds numbers of about 1 to 10, when inertial effects become significant.

soil-water-243.q: What is the premise of a soil inference system?
soil-water-243.a: That a soil's basic properties are enough to infer all its other physical and chemical properties, through logically linked pedotransfer functions.

soil-water-234.q: How do soil-based irrigation controllers decide when to water?
soil-water-234.a: They either skip a timed cycle when the soil is wet or start watering only when moisture falls to a set threshold.

soil-phys-212.q: In the Netherlands, how large is the winter drainage requirement, and where does it come from?
soil-phys-212.a: About 180 mm: 720 mm of precipitation against 540 mm of evaporation.

soil-env-129.q: Why can thawing permafrost add to climate change?
soil-env-129.a: Dead biomass has built up in it over millennia without fully decomposing; as warming thaws it, decomposition restarts and releases carbon dioxide or methane.

soil-phys-184.q: Which changes temperature more over a day: a material of low or high thermal effusivity?
soil-phys-184.a: One of low effusivity; a material of high effusivity changes much less.

soil-chem-191.q: What can electron probe microanalysis reveal inside a mineral grain?
soil-chem-191.a: Chemical zoning from core to rim, which records the grain's history.

soil-chem-111.q: Why can ferrihydrite hold so much arsenic, lead or phosphate?
soil-chem-111.a: Its nanoporous particles give several hundred square metres of surface per gram, which adsorb these substances.

soil-chem-164.a: When iron-bearing substances rust underwater, and commonly where primary iron minerals weather.

soil-chem-146.q: What does the Langmuir isotherm assume about a surface?
soil-chem-146.a: Equivalent sites holding one molecule each, an energetically uniform surface and at most a monolayer, assumptions seldom all true.

soil-chem-205.q: How does surface heterogeneity explain the Freundlich equation?
soil-chem-205.a: High-energy sites fill first, then low-energy ones, so the heat of adsorption weakens with coverage.

soil-chem-124.a: With a platinum electrode, read relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

soil-chem-014.q: How does controlled drainage save irrigation water?
soil-chem-014.a: Where wet and dry seasons are marked, drains run only in the wet season.

soil-chem-043.q: In the Maas–Hoffman model, what is the breakpoint?
soil-chem-043.a: The salinity up to which yield is unaffected; beyond it, yield falls.

soil-bio-217.a: In two stages: its hyphae secrete enzymes that break polymers into small units such as monomers, which are then absorbed.

soil-bio-059.q: How do bacteria such as Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans cause acid mine drainage?
soil-bio-059.a: They use iron sulfide to generate sulfuric acid, which drains from the mine with runoff and can drive the pH of groundwater and streams down to 2–3.

soil-bio-205.q: How does a chemoautotroph differ from a chemoheterotroph?
soil-bio-205.a: A chemoautotroph builds all its organic compounds from carbon dioxide; a chemoheterotroph, like most animals and fungi, cannot fix carbon into its own organic compounds.

soil-bio-209.q: Why can microarthropod communities be used as bioindicators?
soil-bio-209.a: They are very sensitive to changes in ecosystems.

soil-bio-166.q: How widespread is arbuscular mycorrhiza among plants?
soil-bio-166.a: It is the most widespread plant symbiosis known, found in about 80% of plant species, on every continent except Antarctica.

soil-bio-181.q: What do endophytic fungi give a plant in exchange for carbohydrates?
soil-bio-181.a: They can increase its water or nutrient uptake and protect it from insects, birds or mammals.

soil-bio-252.q: How does a rhizotron let researchers watch roots?
soil-bio-252.a: A central corridor usually has viewing windows into the soil profiles on either side.

soil-bio-131.q: Which kind of kerogen yields oil, which yields gas, and which yields none?
soil-bio-131.a: Labile kerogen yields mainly oil, refractory kerogen mainly gas, and inert kerogen no hydrocarbons but graphite.

soil-bio-253.q: Why do bacteria and fungi release exoenzymes into their surroundings?
soil-bio-253.a: Breaking macromolecules into small pieces lets their constituents pass through the cell membrane and be used inside the cell.

soil-class-001.q: What traits do soil classification systems group soils by?
soil-class-001.a: Measurable traits such as texture, structure, mineral composition and the way the soil formed.

soil-class-044.q: Why were human-made soils long left out of classification systems?
soil-class-044.a: Criteria built for natural soils often do not apply to them.

soil-class-093.q: What is the defining trait of an Aridisol?
soil-class-093.a: Water deficiency: an aridic moisture regime, with fewer than 90 consecutive moist days in the growing season, and no leaching.

soil-class-131.q: Which Leptosols are the most extensive on Earth?
soil-class-131.a: Lithic Leptosols, less than 10 cm deep, in mountain regions.

soil-class-058.q: What gives red soils their colour?
soil-class-058.a: High iron content, which gives colours from reddish brown to reddish yellow.

soil-fert-175.q: How does potassium help a plant tolerate drought?
soil-fert-175.a: It opens and closes stomata through an ion pump, so it controls water loss from leaves.

soil-fert-171.q: How much of a plant's dry mass is carbon?

soil-fert-146.q: How does a nutrient cycle differ from the flow of energy through an ecosystem?
soil-fert-146.a: Energy flows one way through ecosystems, but mineral nutrients cycle.

soil-fert-125.q: What did a 15-year nitrogen-addition study at Harvard Forest find?
soil-fert-125.a: More leaching, higher pine mortality and an end to biomass accumulation.

soil-fert-030.q: Which compost organisms are the most abundant and important?
soil-fert-030.a: Bacteria, which excrete plant-available nitrogen, phosphorus and magnesium; mesophilic or thermophilic kinds dominate depending on the phase.

soil-fert-209.q: Why did demand for guano fall rapidly after 1910?

soil-fert-215.q: What does wood ash supply as a fertilizer?
soil-fert-215.a: Potassium, and calcium carbonate, which acts as a liming agent to neutralise acid soils.

soil-fert-040.q: How does phosphate rich organic manure free the phosphorus locked in rock phosphate?
soil-fert-040.a: Microbial organic acids slowly dissolve its insoluble tricalcium phosphate, and the organic matter stops other ions locking the phosphorus into insoluble forms.

soil-water-021.q: Why does saturation-excess overland flow start sooner after earlier rain?
soil-water-021.a: Antecedent soil moisture sets how soon soil saturates: the wetter it starts, the sooner runoff begins.

soil-water-036.q: How are unpaved lots and dirt roads kept from raising dust?
soil-water-036.a: They are paved or gravelled, or stabilized with water, vegetable oil, calcium chloride or other suppressants.

soil-water-049.q: What share of eroded sediment reaches rivers in Europe, according to WaTEM/SEDEM estimates?
soil-water-049.a: About 15%: that is the estimated sediment delivery ratio.

soil-water-284.q: How can as little as 1 mm of silt harm coral?
soil-water-284.a: Suspended sediment disrupts filter-feeding organisms and deposits bury them; 1 mm of accumulation may kill coral polyps.

soil-water-249.q: How does bed load move along a stream?
soil-water-249.a: It rolls, slides and hops along the bed at a small fraction of the flow speed.

soil-water-069.q: How do roots crossing a potential failure plane stabilize a slope?
soil-water-069.a: They raise shear strength by binding particles and anchor unstable surface soil to deeper stable layers or bedrock.

soil-water-293.q: Why does an alluvial fan form where a channel opens out?
soil-water-293.a: Flow leaving a confined channel spreads out and loses the capacity to carry its sediment.

soil-water-120.q: How does the National Technical Committee for Hydric Soils define a hydric soil?
soil-water-120.a: As soil formed under saturation, flooding or ponding long enough to turn its upper part anaerobic.

soil-agri-150.q: Why does burning the slash raise soil fertility for a time?
soil-agri-150.a: It leaves a nutrient-rich ash layer and temporarily removes weeds and pests.

soil-agri-145.q: How does expanded clay aggregate help a heavy soil?
soil-agri-145.a: Mixed in, its pellets improve aeration and drainage.

soil-agri-124.q: Why does keyline cultivation give water more time to infiltrate?
soil-agri-124.a: Cultivating parallel to the keyline drifts runoff away from the valley centre, delaying runoff concentration.

soil-agri-063.q: How do reduced-tillage and no-till systems protect soil?
soil-agri-063.a: They keep residues on the surface for erosion protection and water retention.

soil-agri-068.q: What does a catch crop do with nitrogen left from the previous crop?
soil-agri-068.a: It takes up the surplus, keeping it from loss by leaching, denitrification or volatilization, and returns it to the soil when worked in as green manure or decomposed.

soil-agri-094.q: Why can a single poor rating make a Storie index zero?
soil-agri-094.a: The index multiplies its ratings, so a zero in any one makes the whole result zero.

soil-meth-018.q: In the WRB, what does the whole soil include besides the fine earth?
soil-meth-018.a: Coarse fragments, artefacts, cemented parts and dead plant residues of any size.

soil-meth-002.q: What are the nugget, sill and range of a variogram?
soil-meth-002.a: The nugget is a jump at the origin, the sill its limit at large distances, and the range the distance where it nears the sill.

soil-env-275.q: What mainly decides the net methane flux from a wetland?
soil-env-275.a: How much methane made by methanogens reaches the surface before methanotrophs oxidize it.

soil-env-100.q: What sets the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification apart from other agreements on land?
soil-env-100.a: It is the only internationally legally binding framework on desertification, and the only convention stemming directly from the Rio Conference's Agenda 21.

soil-env-080.q: What happens to people when desertified rural land can no longer support them?
soil-env-080.a: They migrate to cities, particularly in Africa, creating unemployment and slums.

soil-env-311.q: What caused the spoil tip at Aberfan, Wales, to collapse in 1966?
soil-env-311.a: It was built over a spring and saturated by heavy rain; it collapsed onto a school, killing 144 people.

soil-env-200.q: How does PFAS in soil reach people?
soil-env-200.a: Crops take it up: soil contamination raises PFAS in foods such as white rice, coffee and animals reared on the land.

soil-env-017.q: Why are coliform bacteria in runoff measured if they do not cause disease?
soil-env-017.a: They are a common indicator of water pollution.

soil-env-050.q: What makes a plant a hyperaccumulator?
soil-env-050.a: It concentrates metals to levels toxic to related species not adapted to metalliferous soils, for example over 1000 mg/kg of dry weight for nickel, copper, cobalt, chromium or lead.

soil-env-247.q: How does bioslurping recover oil from above the water table?
soil-env-247.a: A slurp tube reaching into the free-product layer draws up liquid and soil gas together, lifting oil off the water table and capillary fringe.

soil-env-298.q: How did cadmium from upstream mines reach the people who developed itai-itai disease?
soil-env-298.a: Residents irrigated rice with the Jinzū River water, so the highly soluble cadmium contaminated paddies and rice and raised body burdens.

soil-hist-119.q: How do absolute and relative ages differ in the methods that produce them?
soil-hist-119.a: Absolute ages come from radioactive isotopes, while relative ages come from tools such as paleomagnetism and stable isotope ratios.

soil-hist-088.q: Into which two stages does taphonomy divide its processes?
soil-hist-088.a: Biostratinomy, between death and burial, and diagenesis, after burial.

soil-hist-077.q: What does agricultural chemistry often aim to do for soil?
soil-hist-077.a: Preserve or raise soil fertility so as to keep or improve crop yields and crop quality.

soil-hist-001.q: Besides parent material, what did Dokuchaev show explains how soil types vary from place to place?
soil-hist-001.a: Climate, topography and the length of soil formation.

soil-hist-076.q: What did a failed royal commission on truffle cultivation lead Albert Bernhard Frank to discover?
soil-hist-076.a: The nature and development of mycorrhizae, which he named in an 1885 paper.

soil-hist-069.q: What level of perchlorate in Martian regolith is considered toxic to humans?
soil-hist-069.a: Around 0.5%, and even trace amounts interfere with human thyroid function.
